name: Subway tile
region: New York, USA, and then the whole world
summary: A small white rectangular wall tile with a glossy glaze and a bevelled edge, laid in a brick bond. It began as a clean, washable lining for tunnels and stations. It is now the default tile of the kitchen and the bathroom.

philosophy.core_thesis: A white, shiny, small tile makes a wall that is clean, bright and easy to wash.
design_principles: Make the tile a 2:1 rectangle, 3 by 6 inches, or about 7.5 by 15 cm.
Use a white glaze with a high gloss, 85 to 100 GU, so that the wall reflects light.
Bevel the edge by 1 to 2 mm, so that each tile has a soft line and the grout is not flat.
Lay the tiles in a running bond with a half-tile offset, and keep the joints to 2 to 3 mm.
Fill the joint with a light or a dark grout in one colour to set the strength of the grid.
Add a trim set: a bullnose, a cap, a base and a corner piece in the same glaze.
Keep the wall plain; use one band of colour or one border at most.
Fire the tile hard enough that the glaze does not craze and stains do not enter.
anti_patterns: A rough, hand-made surface with a wavy edge
A printed pattern on each tile
A square tile in a stack bond for a classic look
A deep relief that holds dirt
A dull matt glaze with large pores

form.shape: Small rectangular wall tiles in white, with trim pieces: bullnose, cap, base and corner.
form.profile: A flat face with a slight bevel on all four edges; a bullnose has a rounded edge.
form.foot_and_rim: The back has a grid of small ribs for the mortar; the edge has a small lug on early tiles to hold the joint.
form.proportion: A standard tile is 3 by 6 inches and 6 to 8 mm thick; a wall uses 140 tiles in each square metre.
rules: Keep the 2:1 ratio so that the running bond lines up.
Make every tile the same size to 0.5 mm, so that the joints stay straight.
Include a trim piece for each edge and corner.

bodies.rule: Use a white or buff pressed earthenware for the wall. Use vitreous china for the tile that stays wet, as in a bath or a pool. Keep fine porcelain out.

methods: pressing the tile from dust in a steel die
dipping or spraying in a white glaze
setting the tile in a glaze kiln on a roller
bevelling the edge in the die
forming.joins: The tile is set in a cement bed or in adhesive, and the joints are filled with grout.
forming.details: A slight bevel, small ribs on the back, a clean edge and a mark of the maker.

glaze.pattern: No pattern. A plain white gloss, or one colour in the same gloss; a moulded bullnose or cap in the same glaze.
glaze.wear: The glaze wipes clean for decades; fine cracks in the glaze let in dirt, and the edge chips in a wet room.

palette.strategy: White first; one or two soft colours from the same glaze family; the grout sets the line.

firing.kiln: A tunnel kiln or a roller kiln.
firing.scale: A line makes tens of thousands of tiles in a day and covers the interior of whole stations.
firing.signs: A uniform gloss, small bevels, a very slight wave in the glaze and ribs on the back.

emotion.target_response: A bright, clean ease: the viewer sees a wall that is easy to wash and has no fuss.

use_cases: a plain white wall with a strong grid
avoid_when: the brief needs a painted or printed pattern
the brief needs a hand-made look
the brief needs a floor with relief

modifiers.how: Use a slab of 60 by 120 cm in a matt porcelain stoneware with fine joints.
Add a curved plant relief and a soft matt glaze in muted green.
